habitat: The colour key places it at wetlands. The description paragraph on the same page is about a different bird and is not used for habitat.
summary: The colour key, headed Merops persicus, says it is entirely green above, with pale blue eyebrows, cheeks and belly, a yellow chin and a rufous throat. The description on that page is a rare vagrant with pink underparts and slate-grey upperparts, recorded at Cape Recife, and does not match this colour key, so it is not used. No status or months are stored. Newman’s matching text does not describe a call. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged.

calls.description: The colour key does not describe a call, and the call sentence on the page sits in the mismatched description, so it is not used. Grade A call from Karaulbazar District, Bukhara Province, Uzbekistan. The filename is XC133400-Blue_cheeked Bee_eater_R1_0029.mp3.

research.note: The Newman description paragraph does not match the Merops persicus colour key, so that paragraph’s plumage and call are not used. Only the colour key and the size are applied. Population figures and the Kemp code NB were left unchanged. Status is palearctic-migrant: SABAP1 calls it a Palearctic migrant with no confirmed austral winter records.

similar.note: Southern Carmine Bee-eater is carmine-red with a blue crown and a pink throat, not green with blue cheeks.
